thread:
jessie: Quick heads-up — hit a perf cliff on a customer node (sm92) when sequence length crosses ~1024. Runtime flips to the generic kernel path and latency doubles. Posting probe output and a short profiling snippet.

raj: Can you paste the device_probe output and the stack of kernel choices?

jessie: Sure — probe summary: 
```
device_probe: gpu0
sm: 92
tensor_cores: yes
bf16_support: 1
fp8_support: 0
driver: 537.88
kernel_order_seen: [fastpath_seqlen_hint, generic_kv_unified, bf16_accel]
seqlen_histogram: {"<256":0.2, "256-512":0.5, "512-1024":0.2, ">1024":0.1}
```
Also microbench (single-stream, p50): seqlen=512 -> 36ms, seqlen=1024 -> 105ms (jump happens when runtime selects generic_kv_unified).

anya: Oof. That sounds like our seqlen-gating logic isn't honoring the tensor-core/bf16 path for sm92. We should prefer bf16_accel when bf16_support && tensor_cores, even for borderline seqlen buckets.

sam: Agreed. Current autodetect looks like: 1) detect SM, 2) pick path by seqlen threshold, 3) fallback by kernel availability. We need a score-based pick instead of strict thresholds: score = w1*seqlen_penalty + w2*cap_bonus + w3*kv_cache_penalty.

ciara: Can you add the KV cache behavior? Why does generic_kv_unified get chosen — is kv cache compatibility broken on the bf16 path?

jessie: Good catch — for large sequences our KV cache allocator falls back to a non-contiguous layout, which currently marks bf16_accel as "incompatible" due to pointer alignment assumptions. So the kernel picker excludes it. That's a bug in kvcache-layout detection.

raj: Two parts then: (A) fix kvcache layout compatibility so bf16_accel remains eligible, (B) change kernel selection to a weighted score with a per-arch cap_bonus. Proposed caps: sm>=90 -> cap_bonus +20; tensor_cores true -> +15; bf16_support true -> +10. seqlen_penalty = floor(seqlen/256)*-8. If score >= 0 prefer fastpath_accel.

anya: Sounds reasonable. Also add a small hysteresis to avoid flipping on noisy histograms (require >10% samples in bucket to flip).

sam: For rollout: feature-flag the scorer and add perf guardrails. We can A/B on Dedicated hosts — gauge p50/p95 and per-token cost. Create INF ticket.

ciara: What numbers should we expect if we enable preferred scoring on sm92? I re-ran a quick synthetic: seqlen=1024 throughput tokens/s: generic_kv_unified=18k tps, bf16_accel (fixed kvcache) = 31k tps. p50 latency: generic=105ms, bf16_accel=62ms.

jessie: Nice. I'll open INF-8342 with the kvcache layout patch + kernel scorer PR. Also adding a unit test that simulates non-contiguous kv layout and validates compatibility tag stays set.

probe-bot: device_probe ran on node host-17 at 2003456760: [sm=92 tensor_cores=yes bf16=1 fp8=0 driver=537.88]

raj: For the PR, pls include a small matrix of driver/firmware combos — we saw earlier subtle bf16 math differences on driver 540.x that required a fallback. Add a guard to mark bf16_accel unstable on driver >=540 && <542.

jessie: Will do. Plan: patch kvcache layout detection (today), add scorer + config flag (tomorrow), unit tests + integration microbench (day after). Rollout by canary to Dedicated fleet, monitor p50/p95 and kv cache hit ratio.

anya: Also confirm that the runtime exposes the chosen kernel in traces to make postmortem debugging easier. Add a trace field kernel_choice and score_breakdown.

ciara: Thx — ping me when INF-8342 PR is up, I'll run Bench-suite and smoke-check on our sm86/92/100 matrix.

jessie: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/changes/INF-8342, includes benchmark log and proposed weights.

sam: lgtm, but keep an eye on memory overhead — bf16_accel uses slightly different kv stride. If memory jumps, we need a cap to avoid OOM on small VMs.

jessie: noted. Adding memory_guard parameter to scorer (max_kv_bytes_percent).
